terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Blue screen of death (BSOD)
terms.definition: Windows stops with a blue screen when bad hardware, bad drivers, or a failing app prevents the OS from continuing. Note the stop code / QR details for targeting the right fix.
terms.scenario: Windows stops on a blue screen with a stop code after a bad driver, bad hardware, or a failing app. What crash is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Last Known Good Configuration
terms.definition: Boot into the last successful startup registry and driver set after a bad driver or config change.
terms.scenario: A user changed a registry setting last night to enable a feature, and now the PC won't boot past a blue screen. They don't know exactly which setting broke it. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: System Restore
terms.definition: Roll system files, drivers, and settings back to a restore point without wiping personal documents.
terms.scenario: A BSOD started after installing an unknown third-party utility a few days ago, and the user doesn't remember exactly what else they changed. They want to undo recent system-wide changes without losing their documents. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Roll back drivers
terms.definition: In Device Manager, undo a recently installed driver that started the crashes.
terms.scenario: BSODs started right after updating a specific GPU driver. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Safe Mode
terms.definition: Boot with only essential drivers/services so you can remove bad software or roll back drivers that block a normal start.
terms.scenario: The PC blue-screens every time it boots normally, and you need to get in to uninstall a bad app or roll back a driver. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Reseat components
terms.definition: Power down and reseat RAM, GPU, and power connectors — loose hardware often looks like a software stop error.
terms.scenario: A desktop was just moved to a new desk, and now it randomly blue-screens with no software changes made. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Hardware diagnostics
terms.definition: Run UEFI/BIOS or vendor tools to test CPU and RAM when stop codes point at memory or kernel faults.
terms.scenario: The BSOD stop code specifically references a memory or kernel fault, and reseating components didn't help. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Boot issues
terms.definition: Windows fails to start normally — missing OS/bootloader, dual-boot conflicts, or the system only reaches Safe Mode. Non-bootable media can also block startup.
terms.scenario: Windows fails to start normally — missing bootloader, dual-boot conflict, leftover media, or it only reaches Safe Mode. What class of problem is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Remove non-bootable media
terms.definition: Unplug USB installers, external drives, and optical discs that the firmware may try to boot before the OS disk.
terms.scenario: A laptop won't boot past the firmware screen, and there's a USB installer stick still plugged in from a reimage last week. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Startup Repair
terms.definition: Use the automated WinRE tool first when Windows fails to start or only boots into Safe Mode.
terms.scenario: Windows fails to start normally and only reaches Safe Mode, with no problematic media plugged in. What's the first tool to try?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: bootrec /rebuildbcd
terms.definition: From the Recovery Console, rebuild the Boot Configuration Database when Startup Repair is not enough.
terms.scenario: Startup Repair ran but couldn't fix the boot problem. What's the next step?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: “No OS found”
terms.definition: The firmware or bootloader cannot find a bootable OS — often bootloader corruption, dual-boot overwrites, or missing boot files.
terms.scenario: Firmware or the bootloader cannot find a bootable operating system. What message is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Unplug non-bootable drives
terms.definition: Disconnect extra media and secondary disks so firmware boots the correct Windows volume.
terms.scenario: A tech just added a second (non-bootable, data-only) internal drive to a desktop, and now firmware shows "No OS found" on restart. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Startup Repair
terms.definition: Let WinRE repair missing or damaged boot files that trigger a “No OS found” message.
terms.scenario: "No OS found" appears, no extra media is connected, and boot files seem to be missing or damaged. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: bootrec /rebuildbcd
terms.definition: Manually rebuild the BCD from the Recovery Console command prompt if Startup Repair does not restore boot.
terms.scenario: Startup Repair didn't resolve the "No OS found" error. What's the next step?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Degraded performance
terms.definition: The PC feels slow or unresponsive — apps lag, disk thrashing is high, or tasks take longer than normal.
terms.scenario: The PC feels slow or unresponsive — apps lag and tasks take longer than normal. What symptom is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Task Manager
terms.definition: Use Processes and a ~60-second Performance view to find the apps consuming CPU, disk, or memory.
terms.scenario: A PC feels slow and you don't yet know why — you want to identify which specific app or process is hogging CPU, disk, or memory. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Windows Update checks
terms.definition: Install pending OS patches that fix known performance bugs and resource leaks.
terms.scenario: The PC has been sluggish for weeks and hasn't installed updates in months. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Free disk space
terms.definition: Clear unused files so the volume has headroom for paging, updates, and temp files.
terms.scenario: The C: drive is at 98% full and the PC is sluggish, especially during updates and multitasking. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Defrag (HDD)
terms.definition: On hard disks, run Optimize/Defragment. Skip routine defrag on SSDs — they use TRIM/optimize instead.
terms.scenario: An older PC with a traditional spinning hard drive (not an SSD) feels slow opening files. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Laptop power source
terms.definition: Seat the charger firmly — on battery or a weak adapter, Windows may throttle the CPU.
terms.scenario: A laptop is fast when plugged in but noticeably sluggish on battery. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Antivirus scan
terms.definition: Run a full scan when Task Manager shows unexplained high CPU or disk use from malware.
terms.scenario: Task Manager shows unexplained high CPU and disk usage from a process the user doesn't recognize. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Low memory warnings
terms.definition: Windows warns that memory is nearly full — apps may freeze, crash, or refuse to open while RAM pressure is high.
terms.scenario: Windows warns that RAM is nearly full; apps freeze, crash, or refuse to open. What warning is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Close memory-heavy apps
terms.definition: Sort Task Manager by Memory, save work, then close or restart the programs using the most RAM.
terms.scenario: RAM usage is high, apps are freezing, and the user has time to sort through what's open and close the worst offenders without losing work. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Virtual memory (paging file)
terms.definition: Review the paging file under System > About > Advanced system settings > Performance Settings > Virtual Memory.
terms.scenario: RAM is consistently near capacity as a longer-term pattern (not just once), and you want to review how Windows is managing overflow to disk. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Frequent shutdowns
terms.definition: The system powers off or stops without a scheduled shutdown — often hardware faults, corrupted system files, or malware.
terms.scenario: The PC powers off with no scheduled shutdown. What symptom is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Full hardware diagnostics
terms.definition: Test motherboard, CPU, and RAM with UEFI/BIOS or vendor diagnostic tools.
terms.scenario: A desktop shuts off randomly with no clear cause, and no component has been tested yet. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Windows Memory Diagnostics
terms.definition: Reboot into the built-in RAM test when random power-offs suggest memory errors.
terms.scenario: Random shutdowns are happening and you specifically suspect faulty RAM. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: System File Checker (sfc)
terms.definition: Run sfc /scannow to repair corrupted Windows files that can force unexpected stops.
terms.scenario: Random shutdowns are happening and Windows system files may be corrupted. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Anti-malware scan
terms.definition: Scan for malware that can crash services or force the machine offline.
terms.scenario: A PC shuts down unexpectedly and you suspect malware is crashing a system service. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: System instability
terms.definition: Random crashes, freezes, or reboots with no single app clearly to blame.
terms.scenario: Random crashes, freezes, or reboots with no single app clearly to blame. What symptom is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Full hardware diagnostics
terms.definition: Stress-test CPU, RAM, and related hardware when there is no clear software cause.
terms.scenario: Random crashes and freezes happen with no clear app to blame, and no hardware testing has been done yet. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Windows Memory Diagnostics
terms.definition: Run the built-in RAM test when freezes or BSODs look memory-related.
terms.scenario: Freezes and BSODs look memory-related. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: System File Checker (sfc)
terms.definition: Scan and repair corrupted Windows system files with sfc /scannow.
terms.scenario: The system is unstable and core Windows files may be damaged. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Anti-malware scan
terms.definition: Scan for malware that injects into processes or tampers with system files.
terms.scenario: The system is unstable and you suspect something has injected into running processes. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Time drift
terms.definition: The clock slowly loses accuracy because of unreliable hardware timekeeping — which can break auth, certificates, and sync.
terms.scenario: The clock slowly loses minutes, and HTTPS certs or Kerberos start failing. What problem is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Set time automatically
terms.definition: In Settings > Time & Language > Date & Time, enable automatic time (and DST) so Windows syncs to time servers, or sync manually.
terms.scenario: Every HTTPS site throws a certificate warning on one laptop only — other devices on the same network are fine. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Services not starting
terms.definition: Windows or third-party services fail to start, leaving features offline until drivers, permissions, or dependencies are fixed.
terms.scenario: Print Spooler or another Windows service never comes up after reboot. What symptom is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Device Manager
terms.definition: Check device status, then update, roll back, or replace drivers that block related services.
terms.scenario: A service won't start, and you suspect it's tied to a piece of hardware whose driver may need updating or rolling back. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: services.msc
terms.definition: Start the service manually, adjust the log-on account, and verify dependencies in the Services app.
terms.scenario: A service shows "Stopped," Device Manager shows no driver issues, and you suspect a wrong log-on account or unmet dependency. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: sfc /scannow
terms.definition: Repair corrupted built-in Windows service binaries. For third-party app services, reinstall the app with admin rights.
terms.scenario: A built-in Windows service won't start because its binary appears corrupted. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Applications crashing
terms.definition: One or more programs close unexpectedly, hang, or fail to stay open during normal use.
terms.scenario: One program keeps closing, hanging, or refusing to stay open. What symptom is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Event Viewer / Reliability Monitor
terms.definition: Inspect crash logs and reliability history to identify the failing module or recent change.
terms.scenario: An app keeps crashing and you don't yet know why. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Reinstall the application
terms.definition: Repair or reinstall the failing app after logs point to a corrupted install.
terms.scenario: Logs point to a corrupted install as the cause of an app's crashes. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: USB controller resource warnings
terms.definition: Connecting a device exceeds the USB controller’s available endpoints, so Windows warns or the device misbehaves.
terms.scenario: Plugging in a USB device triggers a warning that the controller is out of endpoints. What warning is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Move to another USB port
terms.definition: Disconnect the device and plug it into a different port or controller to free endpoints.
terms.scenario: Plugging in one more USB device triggers a "not enough resources" warning on a hub with several devices already connected. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Balance USB 2.0 / 3.0
terms.definition: Keep USB 2.0 devices on USB 2.0 controllers and USB 3.0 devices on USB 3.0 controllers to spread endpoint load.
terms.scenario: USB endpoint warnings keep happening because USB 2.0 and 3.0 devices are all crammed onto the same controller. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Slow profile load
terms.definition: Sign-in takes a long time, usually from network latency or WAN congestion while syncing a roaming profile to a domain controller.
terms.scenario: Domain sign-in takes a long time while a roaming profile syncs, but once it finishes the desktop is normal. What symptom is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Repair / optimize domain controllers
terms.definition: Domain admins fix or optimize local DCs and profile sync paths so roaming profiles load without WAN bottlenecks.
terms.scenario: Sign-in takes a very long time over the WAN, but once it finishes, all the user's normal files and settings are there correctly. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Rebuild user profile
terms.definition: A corrupted or temporary profile shows a default wallpaper and empty Documents after a fast domain logon. Rename C:\Users\username, delete that profile's SID under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList, sign in again, then copy files back from the renamed folder.
terms.scenario: A user reaches the desktop quickly, but it shows default wallpaper and an empty Documents folder. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Application fails to launch
terms.definition: Restart the device. Update the app. Reinstall the app.
terms.scenario: A phone app will not open at all. After a reboot you update it, then reinstall it. What issue are you working?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Application fails to close / crashes
terms.definition: Force close the app. Restart the device. Update the app. Reinstall the app. Review crash logs / contact support.
terms.scenario: The app is stuck on screen or dies mid-use. You force-close it, reboot, update, then reinstall and check crash logs. What issue is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Application fails to update
terms.definition: Update the app. Check payment method. Check network / try another network. Check storage space. Restart the device. Check MDM policy.
terms.scenario: The store will not patch the app. You check payment, network, storage, reboot, and MDM before trying again. What issue is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Application fails to install
terms.definition: Check storage space. Check payment method. Check network / try another network. Check MDM policy.
terms.scenario: A new app will not install. Storage, payment method, network, and MDM policy are the first checks. What issue is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Slow to respond
terms.definition: Restart the device. Update the app. Update the OS.
terms.scenario: The phone feels laggy in one app. You reboot, then update the app and the OS. What symptom is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: OS fails to update
terms.definition: Check storage space. Check network / try another network. Restart the device.
terms.scenario: The phone OS update will not finish. You free storage, try another network, and reboot. What issue is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Battery life issues
terms.definition: Airplane Mode (poor coverage). Turn off unused radios (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, GPS). Check battery health. Replace the battery.
terms.scenario: The phone dies by lunch. You try Airplane Mode in poor coverage, kill unused radios, then check battery health. What issue is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Random reboots
terms.definition: Update the OS. Update the app. Review crash logs / contact support. Check battery health.
terms.scenario: The phone restarts by itself. You update OS and apps, review crash logs, and check the battery. What symptom is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Connectivity issues — Wi-Fi
terms.definition: Toggle the radio off and on (Wi-Fi / Bluetooth / NFC). Verify Wi-Fi password / AP settings. Check network / try another network. Restart the device.
terms.scenario: The phone will not join the office SSID. You toggle Wi-Fi, recheck the password/AP, try another network, then reboot. What issue is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Connectivity issues — Bluetooth
terms.definition: Toggle the radio off and on (Wi-Fi / Bluetooth / NFC). Restart the device. AirDrop: Bluetooth + Wi-Fi on; move closer.
terms.scenario: Headphones will not pair. You toggle Bluetooth, reboot, and for AirDrop you also turn Wi-Fi on and move closer. What issue is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Connectivity issues — Near-field communication (NFC)
terms.definition: Toggle the radio off and on (Wi-Fi / Bluetooth / NFC). Restart the device. Update linked payment cards.
terms.scenario: Tap-to-pay will not fire. You toggle NFC, reboot, and update the cards in the wallet app. What issue is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Screen does not autorotate
terms.definition: Check orientation lock. Close and reopen the app. Restart the device. Hardware failure — contact support.
terms.scenario: Turning the phone sideways does not rotate the screen. You check orientation lock, reopen the app, then reboot. What issue is that?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Restart the device
terms.definition: Power-cycle the phone or tablet first when an app will not open.
terms.scenario: A user taps an app icon and nothing happens at all — no error, no freeze, nothing else has been changed recently. What's the first, quickest fix to try?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Update the app
terms.definition: Install the pending store update when the app dies right after launch.
terms.scenario: The app opens, then immediately closes itself. The App Store shows a pending update for that app. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Reinstall the app
terms.definition: Remove and reinstall the app after restart and update have already failed.
terms.scenario: The app is already on the latest version, the device has been restarted, and it still won't launch. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Force close the app
terms.definition: Force close: iOS — slide it off the app list; Android — Force Stop, then reopen.
terms.scenario: A banking app is frozen on screen and won't respond to any taps. What's the immediate fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Restart the device
terms.definition: Restart the device after a force-close fails to stop the crash.
terms.scenario: Force closing the app didn't help — it crashes again the moment it's reopened. What's the next fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Update the app
terms.definition: Install the available app update after a restart did not stop the crash.
terms.scenario: The app crashes on launch, restarting the device didn't help, and there's a known update available for the app. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Reinstall the app
terms.definition: Reinstall after update and restart still leave the app crashing.
terms.scenario: The app is fully updated and the device has been restarted, but it still crashes every time. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Review crash logs / contact support
terms.definition: Pull crash logs or contact the vendor when a clean reinstall still fails.
terms.scenario: The app still crashes after a fresh reinstall, and the cause isn't obvious. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check payment method
terms.definition: Fix the store payment method when an update is blocked by a declined card.
terms.scenario: An app update is stuck, and the user's card on file for the App Store/Play Store has expired. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check network / try another network
terms.definition: Switch networks (Wi-Fi vs cellular) when the store download fails on one path.
terms.scenario: An app update keeps failing on cellular data specifically. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check storage space
terms.definition: Free storage so the store can download and unpack the update.
terms.scenario: The device has only 200MB free and an app update is stalling. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Restart the device
terms.definition: Restart after payment, network, and storage already check out.
terms.scenario: Payment, network, and storage are all fine, but the update still won't complete. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check MDM policy
terms.definition: MDM may block that app version — check the management policy.
terms.scenario: A work phone under corporate management won't let a specific app update at all. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check storage space
terms.definition: Free space before a new install can land on the device.
terms.scenario: A new app won't install and the device shows only 50MB of free space. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check payment method
terms.definition: Fix the store payment method when a paid install is declined.
terms.scenario: A paid app won't install because the purchase is being declined. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check network / try another network
terms.definition: Try another network when the install never leaves 0%.
terms.scenario: An app install is stuck at 0% on Wi-Fi. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check MDM policy
terms.definition: MDM allow-lists may block unapproved apps — check policy.
terms.scenario: A company-issued phone blocks installation of an app that isn't on the approved list. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Restart the device
terms.definition: Restart first when an app is sluggish and nothing else has been tried.
terms.scenario: An app has been laggy all day for no clear reason, and no other troubleshooting has been tried yet. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Update the app
terms.definition: Install the pending app update after a restart did not fix lag.
terms.scenario: A restart didn't help, and the app has a known update available in the store. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Update the OS
terms.definition: Update the OS after app update and restart still leave the device sluggish.
terms.scenario: The app is fully updated and the device was restarted, but it's still sluggish — and the device hasn't had an OS update installed in a long time. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check storage space
terms.definition: Free storage so the OS update can download.
terms.scenario: An OS update won't download because the device only has 500MB free. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check network / try another network
terms.definition: Try another network when the OS update fails on one SSID.
terms.scenario: An OS update fails every time on public Wi-Fi. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Restart the device
terms.definition: Restart after storage and network already check out for an OS update.
terms.scenario: Storage and network are both fine, but the OS update still won't install. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Airplane Mode
terms.definition: Turn on Airplane Mode in poor coverage so the radio stops hunting.
terms.scenario: A user is in a rural area with very weak cell signal, and their battery is draining fast because the phone keeps searching for a signal. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Turn off unused radios
terms.definition: Turn off unused Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS radios to save battery.
terms.scenario: A user isn't using Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or GPS right now, but all three are left on and battery is draining faster than usual. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check battery health
terms.definition: Check battery health on an aging phone that no longer lasts the day.
terms.scenario: A two-year-old phone that used to last all day now dies by early afternoon with normal use. What's the fix to check first?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Replace the battery
terms.definition: Replace the battery after health confirms it is worn out.
terms.scenario: Battery health check confirms the battery is significantly degraded (well below original capacity). What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Update the OS
terms.definition: Update the OS when random reboots line up with a stale system build.
terms.scenario: A phone randomly restarts a few times a week, and it hasn't had an OS update in months. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Update the app
terms.definition: Update the suspect app when reboots only happen while it is open.
terms.scenario: Random reboots happen only when one specific app is open, and that app has a pending update. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Review crash logs / contact support
terms.definition: Review crash logs or contact support after OS and app updates fail.
terms.scenario: The OS and the suspect app are both fully updated, but random reboots continue. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check battery health
terms.definition: A worn battery can cause random reboots — check battery health.
terms.scenario: Random reboots happen, and a battery health check shows it's severely degraded. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Toggle the Wi-Fi radio
terms.definition: Toggle Wi-Fi off and on first when it will not join any network.
terms.scenario: A phone shows Wi-Fi is on but won't connect to any network, and no other steps have been tried. What's the first fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Verify Wi-Fi password / AP settings
terms.definition: Recheck the Wi-Fi password and AP settings after a radio toggle fails.
terms.scenario: Toggling Wi-Fi off and on didn't help, and the user isn't 100% sure they typed the router password correctly. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check network / try another network
terms.definition: Try another network to isolate a device problem from this AP.
terms.scenario: The password is confirmed correct, but the connection still fails only on this one network. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Restart the device
terms.definition: Restart the device after Wi-Fi toggle, password, and another network fail.
terms.scenario: Toggling Wi-Fi, rechecking the password, and trying another network all failed. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Toggle the Bluetooth radio
terms.definition: Toggle Bluetooth off and on first when pairing fails.
terms.scenario: A user's Bluetooth headphones won't pair, and nothing else has been tried yet. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Restart the device
terms.definition: Restart after a Bluetooth radio toggle does not restore pairing.
terms.scenario: Toggling Bluetooth didn't fix the pairing issue. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Move closer (AirDrop)
terms.definition: AirDrop needs Bluetooth + Wi-Fi on and the devices close together.
terms.scenario: Two iPhones are 15 feet apart in different rooms and AirDrop won't find each other, though Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are both on. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Toggle the NFC radio
terms.definition: Toggle NFC off and on first when tap-to-pay fails.
terms.scenario: Tap-to-pay isn't working at a terminal, and nothing has been checked yet. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Restart the device
terms.definition: Restart after an NFC toggle does not restore tap-to-pay.
terms.scenario: Toggling NFC didn't fix tap-to-pay. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Update linked payment cards
terms.definition: Update the wallet cards after a reissued card fails tap-to-pay.
terms.scenario: NFC and the radio toggle both check out fine, but the specific card being used for tap-to-pay was recently reissued. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Check orientation lock
terms.definition: Check orientation / rotation lock first.
terms.scenario: A user turns their phone sideways and the screen doesn't rotate — nothing else has been checked. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Close and reopen the app
terms.definition: Close and reopen the app when only that app refuses to rotate.
terms.scenario: Orientation lock is off, but one specific app still won't rotate while others do. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Restart the device
terms.definition: Restart when rotation fails in every app after lock and reopen checks.
terms.scenario: Orientation lock is off and the app was reopened, but rotation still doesn't work in any app. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Hardware failure — contact support
terms.definition: If rotation fails in every app after a restart, the accelerometer/gyroscope may be bad — contact support.
terms.scenario: A restart didn't fix it, and rotation fails across every app. What's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Application source / unofficial application stores
terms.definition: Sideloading from uncurated third-party sources risks malware with access to device data — stick to trusted, centralized stores like Google Play or the Apple App Store.
terms.scenario: A user downloads an APK file from a random website to get a "free" version of a paid app instead of using the Play Store. What's the risk, and what's the recommendation?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Developer mode
terms.definition: Tap the build number seven times under Settings > About Phone — it enables advanced OS access, USB debugging, memory stats, and detailed logging.
terms.scenario: An Android user wants to enable USB debugging and detailed logging for testing. How do they enable it, and what does it grant?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Root access / jailbreak
terms.definition: Jailbreak (iOS) grants complete control over the device and strips away MDM management capabilities, which is what enables the sideloading. Android equivalent: root — triggers an MDM bypass.
terms.scenario: A user on a corporate-managed iPhone wants to install apps outside the App Store, so they jailbreak the device. What happens to the device's management, and what specifically enabled the sideloading?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Unauthorized / malicious application
terms.definition: Unauthorized/malicious application — infected dev environments can inject malicious code or enroll users in paid services without consent; check the download source and verify app legitimacy before installing.
terms.scenario: A user installs an app built using a compromised, unofficial version of a development toolchain (like the XcodeGhost incident), and it secretly signs them up for a paid subscription. What's the underlying risk category, and what should users do before installing apps generally?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Application spoofing
terms.definition: Application spoofing — a malicious app masquerading as a legitimate tool.
terms.scenario: A user installs what looks like a simple QR code scanner app, but it's secretly harvesting contacts and messages in the background. What's this called?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: High network traffic
terms.definition: High network traffic, possibly malware command-and-control or encrypted traffic proxying — track usage with a data-monitoring tool and run a malware scan.
terms.scenario: A user notices their phone's data usage has spiked dramatically overnight with no explanation, and they suspect the device is secretly communicating with a remote server. What's the likely cause, and what should they do?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Degraded response time
terms.definition: Degraded response time — restart the device, close background apps, apply OS/app updates, or as a last resort, factory reset.
terms.scenario: A phone has become sluggish, animations stutter, and the screen is slow to respond — but the cause isn't confirmed yet. What's the troubleshooting order?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Data-usage limit notification
terms.definition: A data-usage limit notification — an early warning sign of background malware exfiltrating data.
terms.scenario: A user gets a notification that they've hit their monthly cellular data cap much earlier than usual, with no change in their normal usage habits. What could this indicate?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Limited internet connectivity
terms.definition: Limited internet connectivity — toggle Wi-Fi or Airplane Mode, restart the device, run a malware scan, or reset network settings (iOS).
terms.scenario: A phone's internet feels slow and unreliable across multiple networks, and the user suspects either malware or a misconfiguration. What are the fixes to try?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: No internet connectivity
terms.definition: No internet connectivity — malware may intentionally block internet access to prevent anti-malware updates or security downloads.
terms.scenario: A phone has zero internet connectivity at all, and the user can't even download a security app to check for malware. What might be causing this deliberately?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: High number of ads
terms.definition: High number of ads — adware or fake ad-blocking malware (e.g., Fake Ads Block) generating ad revenue for attackers.
terms.scenario: A user's phone shows constant pop-up ads even while using unrelated apps, and they recently installed a "free ad blocker" app. What's the likely cause?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Fake security warnings
terms.definition: This is a fake security warning — close the browser window immediately without clicking the prompt.
terms.scenario: While browsing, a pop-up appears saying "Your device is infected — click here to install a security update." What should the user do?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Unexpected application behavior
terms.definition: Unexpected application behavior — typically an app-specific bug; contact the app developer and update to the latest version.
terms.scenario: A specific app keeps crashing, feels unresponsive, has a broken feature, and drains the battery fast — but no other apps are affected. What's the likely cause and fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Leaked personal files / data
terms.definition: Leaked personal files/data — run a malware scan, perform a factory reset, update passwords for cloud services (iCloud, Google Workspace, OneDrive), and enable multi-factor authentication (MFA).
terms.scenario: A user discovers private photos and files from their phone have shown up online, and they're not sure if it was a local infection or their cloud account being compromised. What's the full response?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Xcode (iOS developer mode)
terms.definition: iOS developer mode is managed through Xcode on macOS.
terms.scenario: An iOS developer wants to enable developer mode on an iPhone for app testing. How is that managed?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Unable to access the network
terms.definition: Unable to access the network — malware may block the path so patches and AV tools can't download; run a malware cleaner or wipe and restore from a known-good backup.
terms.scenario: A Windows PC suddenly has no network access, and the user can't download Defender updates or a malware cleaner. What's the likely cause, and what's the fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Desktop alerts
terms.definition: Desktop alerts — rogue browser or web messages impersonating system notifications; block unauthorized sites in browser notification settings, or run a malware scan.
terms.scenario: Pop-ups that look like Windows notifications keep asking the user to extend an antivirus subscription or download software. What's this, and how do you handle it?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: False alerts regarding antivirus protection
terms.definition: False alerts regarding antivirus protection (scareware) — the files can be deleted manually, but wiping the system and restoring from backup is the most reliable fix.
terms.scenario: A full-screen window claims the PC is disabled, names a Trojan spyware file, and shows a phone number to call. What's this, and what's the most reliable fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Altered system or personal files
terms.definition: Altered system or personal files (missing / renamed) — a clear malware indicator; use a dedicated cleaner or wipe and restore from a known-good backup.
terms.scenario: Documents and system binaries were renamed or have vanished from where the user left them. What's the symptom, and what does it indicate?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Unwanted notifications within the OS
terms.definition: Unwanted notifications within the OS — configure them app-by-app under Settings > System > Notifications so spam is off and system alerts stay on.
terms.scenario: Installed apps spam the Windows notification center, but the user still wants critical system alerts. What's this, and where do you control it?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: OS update failures
terms.definition: OS update failures — verify internet access, check firewall or bandwidth caps, then run Windows Update Troubleshooter via Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters.
terms.scenario: Windows Update keeps failing. The PC can browse other websites. What should you check, and which built-in tool do you run?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Random / frequent pop-ups
terms.definition: Random / frequent pop-ups — on a modern browser this usually means malware; run a full scan or restore from a known-good backup.
terms.scenario: Fake app prompts keep appearing even though the browser's pop-up blocker is on. What's this, and what does it usually mean?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Certificate warnings
terms.definition: Certificate warnings — click the lock icon next to the HTTPS URL to inspect issuer, expiration, and other cert details.
terms.scenario: The browser says "Your connection is not private." What warning is that, and how do you inspect the certificate?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Redirection
terms.definition: Redirection — almost always malware sending the browser to an ad or payload site; run an anti-malware scan or wipe and restore from a known-good backup.
terms.scenario: The user types a normal Google search but lands on a junk ad or malware site instead. What's this called, and how do you fix it?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Degraded browser performance
terms.definition: Degraded browser performance — too many tabs, a bloated cache, or malicious JavaScript such as a background crypto miner.
terms.scenario: The browser is sluggish and Task Manager shows 100% CPU on one tab. What's the symptom, and what are common causes?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Inability to access files
terms.definition: Inability to access files — altered permissions or Access Denied on personal documents; treat it as malware and use a cleaner or wipe and restore.
terms.scenario: A user can still see their documents, but opening them returns "Access denied" and the permissions look changed. What's this specifically?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Settings > System > Notifications
terms.definition: Configure notifications app-by-app under Settings > System > Notifications.
terms.scenario: App spam fills the Windows notification center, but the user still needs alerts from system services. Where do you turn the extras off app-by-app?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Windows Update Troubleshooter
terms.definition: Windows Update Troubleshooter — Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters; it detects Update problems and tries to fix them automatically.
terms.scenario: Internet access and firewall rules already check out, but Windows Update still fails. Which built-in tool do you run, and where?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Wipe and restore from backup
terms.definition: Wipe the system and restore from a known-good backup — more reliable than manually deleting scareware files.
terms.scenario: Scareware claims Defender is disabled and wants a support-line call. Deleting the executable didn't fully clean it. What's the most reliable fix?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Click the lock icon
terms.definition: Click (or right-click) the lock icon next to the HTTPS URL to inspect the certificate.
terms.scenario: The browser shows a certificate warning. How do you view who issued the cert and when it expires?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Check domain, CA, or system time
terms.definition: Domain name mismatch, an untrusted Certificate Authority, or an incorrect local date and time.
terms.scenario: Certificate warnings keep appearing on sites that used to work. What are the three common causes to check?

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Update browser / clear cache
terms.definition: Update the browser, clear cookies and cache, review Task Manager resource use, and test the same site in another browser.
terms.scenario: The browser is slow and using a lot of CPU. A malware scan already came back clean. What fixes should you try next?
